newsitem.title: UK: Ladbroke says profits ahead in 1st 4 months.
newsitem.headline: Ladbroke says profits ahead in 1st 4 months.

text.p: British hotels and leisure group Ladbroke Group Plc said on Monday its pre-tax profits for the first four months in 1997 was "significantly ahead" of the year-ago period.
Ladbroke also said its Hilton International unit was currently marketing six associate and two Hilton National hotels that had a book value of 90.6 million stg.
In January, Ladbroke and U.S. group Hilton Hotels Corp (HHC) agreed to reunite the Hilton brand worldwide.
HHC had owned the Hilton name in the U.S., while Ladbroke had held the rights for everywhere else.

Ladbroke said Hilton International had a one-percent increase in overall occupancy in the first four months of the year and an eight-percent increase in revenue per available room (revpar) versus the year-ago period.
In the UK, revpar rose by 13 percent, the firm said.
Ladbroke added that profits at its betting and gaming division were substantially ahead of last year, boosted by new products in the UK.

"The group (overall) has made good progress during the first four months of 1997 and, as anticipated, profit before taxation was significantly ahead," Ladbroke said in a statement, noting that interest costs had been cut due to debt reduction.
Ladbroke's shares rose nine pence to 251 by 1100 GMT.
